title: Americans Are Stressed and Asking AI for Help
paragraphs: Nearly three-quarters of US adults think stress is unavoidable, and something that they just have to "live with." And to make that stress easier to manage, many are asking AI for support.
This is what was found in the 2026 Stress in America survey from the American Psychological Association (APA).
The survey, which included over 3,000 US adults, asked people about their main causes of stress — and it's likely no surprise that money worries topped the list.

Seventy-seven percent of participants said that dealing with the cost of living — including keeping up with their house payments or rent, and paying for groceries — was a significant source of stress in their lives.
Around three-quarters of Americans also said that worries about the future of their country were a big source of stress.

And stress is changing how Americans are living their lives. Almost half of survey participants said they have avoided social events in the past year because of stress, uncertainty or feeling overwhelmed.

Many are looking to AI for help. Forty-nine percent said they have talked to AI like it was a friend, while 47% said they have used AI like a mental health professional. One in 10 said they actually rely on AI more than friends and family for advice.
If stress is truly unavoidable, that may sound like a cheap and easy way to deal with it. But the APA's Arthur C. Evans Jr. isn't so sure.
"Chronic stress can take a serious toll on people's physical and psychological well-being," he said. But he also added, "We should not accept that toll as an inevitable part of everyday life."

He also warned against relying on AI for support, saying that while it might help, it cannot replace trained mental health professionals or the human connection that comes from relationships with family and friends.
